source.author: verg
source.text: Nisus erat portae custos, acerrimus armis, Hyrtacides, comitem Aeneae quem miserat Ida venatrix iaculo celerem levibusque sagittis; it iuxta comes Euryalus, quo pulchrior alter non fuit Aeneadum Troiana neque induit arma, ora puer prima signans intonsa iuventa.
source.text_original: Nisus erat portae custos, acerrimus armis, / Hyrtacides, comitem Aeneae quem miserat Ida / venatrix iaculo celerem levibusque sagittis; / it iuxta comes Euryalus, quo pulchrior alter / non fuit Aeneadum Troiana neque induit arma, / ora puer prima signans intonsa iuventa.
source.text_english: Nisus was the guard of the gate, the fiercest in arms, son of Hyrtacus, whom Ida the huntress had sent as a swift companion to Aeneas with her spear and light arrows; Euryalus, his companion, went beside him, than whom no other of the sons of Aeneas was more handsome, nor did any Trojan put on the arms, a boy with his face first marked by the unshorn bloom of youth.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: non illo certior alter pinguia letifera perfringere colla bipenni.
reuse.text_original: non illo certior alter / pinguia letifera perfringere colla bipenni.
reuse.text_english: no other was more certain than he to shatter the fat lethal necks with a two-edged axe.
